# 2 Baruch Chapter 35 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 35 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 35:1 — "mourned with great mourning / mourned deeply"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I-mourned with-great-mourning" | Preserves the Syriac internal object (cognate accusative) |
| LOGOS | "I mourned with great mourning" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "I mourned deeply" | Simplifies the cognate accusative |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "mourned with great mourning" (EMET/LOGOS). The cognate accusative is a Syriac/Semitic intensifying construction that deserves preservation in English.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Semitic intensification preserved.

---

## 35:4 — "see it openly / see it laid bare"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "when-you-see it-openly" | Literal: Syriac b-galya = openly/in the open |
| LOGOS | "when you see it openly" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "when you see it all laid bare before you" | Expansion for drama |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "see it openly" (EMET/LOGOS). The Syriac adverb b-galya means "openly" and refers to the open vision that follows. PNEUMA's expansion "laid bare" adds drama not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
